hypotheses.text: Microcephaly (HP:0000252) in MAU2-related CdLS (CdLS7) is predominantly postnatal and progressive rather than congenital, with normal birth occipitofrontal circumference (>-2.0 SD) in at least 50% of newborns followed by deceleration to <=-2.5 SD in over 75% of individuals during early childhood.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifying whether cranial growth failure in CdLS7 is congenital (primary) or develops postnatally is essential for differential diagnosis against other cohesinopathies and classical CdLS (CdLS1 due to NIPBL), where microcephaly is frequently present at birth.

evidence.text: Affected individuals carrying heterozygous MAU2 variants display a wide range of phenotypes, from classic CdLS to milder presentations, with short stature and microcephaly described as consistent/major clinical features across the 18 subjects.

source.quote: Affected individuals display a wide range of phenotypes, from classic CdLS to milder presentations, with short stature and microcephaly as consistent features.

evidence.text: In a multidisciplinary review of CdLS cohorts, most individuals showed head circumference measurements below standard curves and below the 5th percentile, consistent with progressive postnatal microcephaly and general somatic growth failure.

hypotheses.text: The severity of microcephaly in MAU2 probands differs significantly by variant mechanism, with truncating/loss-of-function variants resulting in an average OFC z-score of <= -3.0 SD compared to an average OFC z-score between -1.5 SD and -2.5 SD in individuals harboring in-frame missense or deletion variants.
hypotheses.rationale: Parenti et al. established that truncating variants result in MAU2 haploinsufficiency and distinct episignatures compared to in-frame variants that disrupt NIPBL binding; determining whether this molecular dichotomy translates into a quantitative divergence in cranial growth severity tests the genotype-phenotype correlation.

evidence.text: MAU2 in-frame variants predominantly impair NIPBL-MAU2 interaction, whereas truncating variants cause MAU2 haploinsufficiency and lead to NIPBL reduction, producing distinct variant-dependent episignatures and a phenotypic spectrum ranging from classic CdLS to milder forms.

source.title: Pathogenic variants in the cohesin loader subunit MAU2
source.quote: In-frame MAU2 variants predominantly impair NIPBL-MAU2 interaction, whereas truncating variants cause MAU2 haploinsufficiency and lead to NIPBL reduction.

evidence.text: In other cohesinopathy genes such as SMC3, predicted loss-of-function variants produce variable growth and microcephaly phenotypes with overall milder presentations compared to dominant-negative missense variants, indicating that loss-of-function does not universally produce more severe microcephaly in cohesin loader/complex genes.

source.title: Heterozygous loss-of-function SMC3 variants are associated with variable growth and developmental features
source.quote: Comparisons to individuals with SMC3 missense/in-frame indel variants demonstrated an overall milder presentation in pLoF carriers. Furthermore, several individuals harboring pLoF variants in SMC3 were nonpenetrant for growth, developmental, and/or dysmorphic features

hypotheses.text: Microcephaly in CdLS7 is symmetric with generalized somatic growth failure, such that occipitofrontal circumference z-scores correlate positively with height and weight z-scores (r >= 0.70) rather than presenting as isolated disproportionate cranial restriction.
hypotheses.rationale: Distinguishing true primary microcephaly from microcephaly that simply parallels systemic growth retardation determines whether brain growth failure is driven by specific neurodevelopmental arrest or generalized cohesin-mediated cellular growth impairment.

evidence.text: CdLS7 is defined as an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by short stature and microcephaly as concurrent core features, with both growth parameters simultaneously affected.

evidence.text: A heterozygous Mau2 knockout mouse model recapitulates cardinal human phenotypes, specifically exhibiting coordinated growth retardation with reduced body size and microcephaly in vivo.

new_directions.question_text: Across the 18 individual patient entries in the Parenti et al. cohort, what are the exact birth OFC z-scores versus last-evaluation OFC z-scores for each individual patient?
new_directions.rationale: Extracting the raw per-patient longitudinal growth measurements from the primary clinical supplementary tables will definitively establish whether cranial growth failure is progressive postnatally or present congenitally.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence or absence of microcephaly in MAU2 variant carriers segregate with specific MAU2 episignature subtypes (episignature 1 vs episignature 2)?
new_directions.rationale: Parenti et al. identified two distinct episignatures reflecting variant-dependent functional disruptions; determining whether cranial circumference z-scores correlate with these epigenetic profiles will establish biomarker predictive value.
